items.name: Prefix conversion
items.what: Converting values with prefixes (p, n, μ, m, k, M, G, T) to base SI units before substituting.

items.name: Area and volume unit conversion
items.what: Converting squared or cubed units, where the prefix factor is squared or cubed.
items.example: 1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m²; 1 cm³ = 10⁻⁶ m³

items.name: Time conversion
items.what: Minutes, hours and milliseconds to seconds.

items.name: Energy unit conversion
items.what: eV ↔ J, kW h ↔ J.

items.name: Standard form and calculator handling
items.what: Entering and reading very large or small numbers correctly.

items.name: Significant figures and rounding
items.what: Giving answers to an appropriate or stated number of s.f.; not rounding intermediate values.
items.example: Data to 2 s.f. → answer to 2 or 3 s.f.

items.name: Rearranging (linear)
items.what: Making a quantity the subject with one or two simple steps.
items.example: V = IR → I = V/R

items.name: Rearranging with squares and roots
items.what: Rearranging where the unknown is squared, square-rooted or in a denominator.
items.example: Ek = ½mv² → v = √(2Ek/m); A = πd²/4 → d = √(4A/π)

items.name: Combining equations algebraically
items.what: Substituting one equation into another to eliminate a quantity or reach a target form.
items.example: R = ρL/A with A = πd²/4 → R = 4ρL/(πd²)

items.name: Direct proportion and ratio
items.what: Scaling when one quantity changes by a factor and another is proportional to it.
items.example: Double the current → double the drift velocity

items.name: Ratio with powers or inverses
items.what: Scaling through a square, square root or inverse relationship, including linked variables.
items.example: Double amplitude → ×4 intensity; double length at constant volume → ×4 resistance

items.name: Percentages
items.what: Efficiency, percentage change, percentage difference and percentage uncertainty arithmetic.

items.name: Means and averages
items.what: Averaging repeat readings; average speed or force.

items.name: Resolving with trigonometry
items.what: Finding components with sin and cos.
items.example: Horizontal component of 32 N at 50° = 32 cos 50°

items.name: Finding angles
items.what: Inverse trig, angles in triangles, angles to the normal.
items.example: θ = sin⁻¹(sin 40° / 1.5)

items.name: Pythagoras and vector magnitude
items.what: Combining perpendicular components into a resultant.
items.example: Resultant of 3 N and 4 N at right angles = 5 N

items.name: Circle area from a diameter
items.what: Cross-sectional area A = πd²/4 (halve the diameter first).

items.name: Volumes and surface areas
items.what: Cuboids, cylinders and spheres (formulae in the booklet).
items.example: Volume of a sphere = 4/3 πr³

items.name: Straight-line form y = mx + c
items.what: Recognising and using gradient and intercept algebraically.
items.example: V = −rI + ε: gradient −r, intercept ε

items.name: Gradient from a graph or data
items.what: Δy/Δx from a large triangle, with axis multipliers and units.
items.example: Gradient of a v–t graph = acceleration

items.name: Area under a graph
items.what: Triangles, trapezia or counting squares, with the value of one square.
items.example: Area under F–t graph = impulse

items.name: Tangent to a curve
items.what: Drawing a tangent at a point to find an instantaneous rate.
items.example: Instantaneous velocity from a curved s–t graph

items.name: Reading scales and divisions
items.what: Reading graphs, meters and oscilloscope divisions with settings.
items.example: 4 divisions × 2 ms/div = 8 ms period

items.name: Estimation and orders of magnitude
items.what: Sensible assumed values and order-of-magnitude answers.
items.example: Mass of a person ≈ 70 kg

items.name: Signs and directions in one dimension
items.what: Choosing a positive direction and keeping signs consistent.
items.example: Rebound: Δv = −6 − (+8) = −14 m s⁻¹

items.name: Degrees and radians
items.what: Converting and using phase angles in either unit.
items.example: Quarter cycle = 90° = π/2 rad

items.name: Choosing an instrument and its resolution
items.what: Naming the right instrument for a quantity and knowing its resolution.
items.example: Wire diameter: micrometer (0.01 mm), not a ruler

items.name: Measuring technique for a specific quantity
items.what: How to measure accurately: several positions, eye level, from a fixed mark, many cycles.
items.example: Time 10 oscillations and divide by 10

items.name: Variables
items.what: Identifying independent, dependent and control variables and how controls are kept constant.
items.example: Keep the current small so the wire's temperature stays constant

items.name: Range, repeats and number of readings
items.what: Taking enough readings over a wide range, repeating and averaging.
items.example: At least 6 lengths from 10 cm to 80 cm, each repeated

items.name: Safety
items.what: A specific hazard for the set-up and a matching precaution.
items.example: Heavy masses: sandbox or cushion underneath, feet clear

items.name: Circuit set-up
items.what: Drawing or describing circuits with correct meter placement and symbols.
items.example: Ammeter in series, voltmeter across the component

items.name: Plotting and best-fit lines
items.what: Plotting points accurately and drawing a straight or curved best-fit line.
items.example: Plot the missing point within half a small square

items.name: Extracting gradient or intercept
items.what: Reading a gradient or intercept from your own or a given graph.
items.example: x-intercept of KEmax–f graph = threshold frequency

items.name: Choosing what to plot (linearising)
items.what: Deciding axes so a relationship gives a straight line.
items.example: Plot V against 1/λ to find h

items.name: Interpreting gradient and intercept
items.what: Stating what the gradient or intercept equals in terms of the physics and solving for the unknown.
items.example: Gradient of R–L = ρ/A, so ρ = gradient × A

items.name: Uncertainty of a measurement
items.what: Absolute uncertainty from resolution or half the range; percentage uncertainty.
items.example: Readings 2.31–2.35 s → ± 0.02 s

items.name: Combining uncertainties
items.what: Adding percentage uncertainties; multiplying by powers.
items.example: ρ ∝ d²: 2 × % uncertainty in d

items.name: Worst-fit line and gradient uncertainty
items.what: Drawing the steepest or shallowest acceptable line through error bars.
items.example: Uncertainty = |best − worst gradient|

items.name: Consistency with an accepted value
items.what: Comparing a result with a known value using uncertainty or percentage difference.
items.example: Accepted value lies within the error range, so consistent

items.name: Anomalies
items.what: Identifying anomalous results and what to do with them.
items.example: Ignore the point far from the line when drawing it; repeat that reading

items.name: Types of error
items.what: Systematic vs random errors, zero error, parallax, reaction time.
items.example: A non-zero micrometer reading with jaws closed is a zero error

items.name: Limitations and improvements
items.what: Specific weaknesses of a method and specific improvements.
items.example: Use light gates and a data logger instead of a stopwatch for short times

items.name: Knowing a standard practical
items.what: Recalling the set-up and procedure of a required practical.
items.example: Determining resistivity, Young modulus, g, Planck constant from LEDs

items.name: Timing methods
items.what: Light gates, data loggers, video analysis, oscilloscope time-base.
items.example: Reaction time ~0.2 s makes stopwatches poor for short times

items.name: Direct substitution
items.what: Picking one booklet equation and substituting.
items.example: v = fλ with f and λ given

items.name: Recall-only equation
items.what: Using one of the equations not in the booklet.
items.example: Ek = ½mv², W = mg, R = V/I

items.name: Choosing the right equation
items.what: Selecting which equation applies from several plausible ones.
items.example: P = I²R (not P = VI with the supply p.d.) for power in the wire

items.name: Chaining equations
items.what: The output of one equation feeds the next.
items.example: A from d → R from ρL/A → P from V²/R

items.name: Using a given unfamiliar formula
items.what: Applying a formula supplied in the question.
items.example: Drag F = kv² given in the stem

items.name: Deriving or showing a relationship
items.what: Combining equations to prove an expression.
items.example: Show that power = 3I(ε − Ir)

items.name: Knowing when an equation applies
items.what: Conditions such as constant acceleration, series circuit, no air resistance.
items.example: suvat only for constant acceleration

items.name: Define a quantity
items.what: Defining a physical quantity in words.
items.example: Resistivity, work function, refractive index

items.name: State a law or principle
items.what: Stating a named law with its conditions.
items.example: Newton's second law; principle of moments; conservation of momentum

items.name: Explain a term
items.what: Saying what a term means, often in a context.
items.example: What 'coherent' or 'terminal velocity' means here

items.name: Units and base units
items.what: Defining a unit or expressing it in base units.
items.example: The volt as a joule per coulomb; kg m² s⁻³ A⁻¹

items.name: What a graph feature represents
items.what: Meaning of gradients, areas and intercepts of standard graphs.
items.example: Area under v–t = displacement

items.name: Classify
items.what: Sorting into categories.
items.example: Vector or scalar; transverse or longitudinal; elastic or plastic

items.name: How components and materials behave
items.what: Characteristic behaviour you must know.
items.example: LDR and thermistor resistance; filament lamp and diode I–V; ductile vs brittle

items.name: Observations of phenomena
items.what: What is seen in key experiments.
items.example: Photoelectric threshold; electron diffraction rings

items.name: Wave and EM properties
items.what: Properties of waves and the EM spectrum.
items.example: Order and wavelengths of the EM spectrum; sound is longitudinal

items.name: Patterns and configurations
items.what: Standard arrangements.
items.example: Closed end of a tube is a node; harmonic patterns on strings

items.name: Applied-context facts
items.what: Facts about real situations named in the spec.
items.example: Factors affecting thinking and braking distance; drag factors

items.name: Symbols and conventions
items.what: Circuit symbols, conventional current, sign conventions.
items.example: LDR symbol; conventional current opposite to electron flow

items.name: Typical values
items.what: Constants and everyday values not given.
items.example: Reaction time ~0.2 s; speed of sound ~340 m s⁻¹

items.name: Apply a conservation law quantitatively
items.what: Using conservation of energy, momentum or charge in a calculation.
items.example: Momentum before = momentum after to find a speed

items.name: Reason qualitatively from a principle
items.what: Explaining an effect from a principle without numbers.
items.example: Why intensity doesn't change the maximum KE of photoelectrons

items.name: Spot the principle in an unfamiliar setting
items.what: Recognising which principle governs a new situation.
items.example: A rocket or a recoiling gun is momentum conservation

items.name: Force analysis
items.what: Free-body diagrams, resultant force, Newton's laws.
items.example: Forces on a lift cable; terminal velocity

items.name: Equilibrium and moments
items.what: Taking moments and resolving for equilibrium.
items.example: Force from a support on a uniform beam

items.name: Superposition reasoning
items.what: Path difference, phase and resultant displacement.
items.example: Maxima and minima from two loudspeakers

items.name: Photon and particle–wave reasoning
items.what: Using the photon model or de Broglie ideas.
items.example: One photon releases one electron
